summary: The 1939 White Pine tower was taken down in the 1970s; only its L-4 cab survives, moved in 2011 to Running Deer Natural Area, though one register places it at CSU's Environmental Learning Center.

facts.design: Timber tower with an L-4 cab, built 1939 by Civilian Conservation Corps enrollees; only the cab survives
facts.status_note: Only the cab survives; the tower was taken down in the 1970s. Sources disagree on whether the cab is at Running Deer Natural Area (FFLA 2012, Forest Lookouts) or at CSU's Environmental Learning Center (FFLOS).

access.note: Forest Lookouts says the repaired cab opened to the public in 2012. It sits in Running Deer Natural Area, Fort Collins; current hours and the cab's exact location were not confirmed.

events.note: Timber tower with an L-4 cab built by Civilian Conservation Corps enrollees, replacing an earlier crow's nest lookout
Former Fort Collins mayor Doug Hutchinson worked as a lookout here in 1964/65
Tower taken down; the cab was lifted off by an Army Reserve helicopter on November 4, 1978
Cab moved to Lee Martinez City Park in Fort Collins
Cab moved by truck and trailer to Running Deer Natural Area on August 25, 2011
High Park Fire burned over the original foundation on West White Pine Mountain in June 2012; the cab had already moved
Fort Collins work days, with FFLA members, reworked, sanded and stained most of the old structure at the new site
Repaired cabin opened to the public

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register says the tower was taken down in the 1970s; Forest Lookouts dates the cab's removal to November 4, 1978, which fits that range. Both are kept.

corrections.field: events: relocated (Moved from White Pine to Running Deer Natural Area, year unknown)
corrections.current: Moved from White Pine to Running Deer Natural Area, year unknown
corrections.proposed: Only the L-4 cab moved to Running Deer Natural Area, on August 25, 2011; the tower itself was taken down in the 1970s and the cab had gone to Lee Martinez City Park in 1978
corrections.why: The record implies the whole tower moved and gives no year. The sources say only the cab moved, twice.

notes_for_editor: Two register-level claims conflict on where the cab is today: FFLOS says CSU's Environmental Learning Center, while the 2012 FFLA report and Forest Lookouts say Running Deer Natural Area. The story reports both and leaves the status 'standing' for the cab. The City of Fort Collins Running Deer page returned no text when fetched, and a search snippet gives a 1967 removal date that could not be checked against the page, so neither is used. Hiker and booking pages were not used. No photos added; the 2016 Coloradoan gallery was seen only in search results.
